rationale: The cardholder's reply settles the open question: they deny the $292.36 online charge (txn 3478782), say it is far above their usual sub-$50 online spend, and do not recognise the hotmail.com contact address on the transaction. That aligns with the objective signals: the amount is 6.55x the 180-day mean ($44.66), above the card's all-time max ($121.32), an amount z of ~9.8, on a card whose history is 100% online/product C at small ticket sizes. Memory also records a prior confirmed CNP fraud on this exact card (CC-4160, $90.54, same customer), so the card number has been exposed before. The semantically similar cases (CC-2537, CC-3639 etc.) were all cleared only because the cardholder confirmed; here the opposite happened, so they cut the other way. The rare device profile 'Trident/7.0 | ie 11.0 for tablet' does link to heavily fraud-affected cards, but it is also 8 of this card's own 35 baseline transactions and appears on 46 cards all-time, so I treat it as a common browser string rather than proof of a shared origin.
